identity.title: Temperature, Mass, and Turbulence: A Spatially Resolved Multiband Non-LTE Analysis of CS in TW Hya

paper_type_evidence.quote: The new observations were part of the ALMA project 2016.1.00440.S, targeting the $(7-6)$ and $(3-2)$ rotational transitions of CS at 342.882850 GHz and 146.969029 GHz in Bands 7 and 4, respectively.

evidence.quote: TW Hya, the nearest protoplanetary disk at $d = 60.1$ pc (cite: Bailer-Jones_ea_2018) with a near face-on inclination of $i \approx 6\ensuremath{^\circ}$.
TW Hya, the nearest protoplanetary disk at $d = 60.1$ pc (cite: Bailer-Jones_ea_2018) with a near face-on inclination of $i \approx 6\ensuremath{^\circ}$.

question.value: What are the temperature, CS column density, H2 density and non-thermal broadening in the TW Hya disk, derived from three CS transitions, and what minimum disk mass do they imply?

evidence.quote: We present an analysis of CS in TW Hya using the $J=7-6$, $5-4$ and $3-2$ transitions imaged at $\sim 0.5\ensuremath{''}$ spatial resolution
The new observations were part of the ALMA project 2016.1.00440.S
Band 6 data comes from project 2013.1.00387.S, originally published in (cite: Teague_ea_2016).

method.value: Provided scripts, phase self-cal, CLEAN with Keplerian mask, different weighting/taper per band to match beams

method.value: Fit Keplerian pattern to first moment maps

evidence.quote: we fit a Keplerian rotation pattern, $v_{\rm Kep} = \sqrt{GM_{\star} \, / \, r}$ to the first moment maps.
The disk centre, $(x_0,\, y_0)$, inclination $i$, position angle, PA and systemic velocity, $v_{\rm LSR}$, were allowed to vary.
The stellar mass was fixed at $0.65~M_{\rm sun}$ (cite: Qi_ea_2004)

method.value: Shift each pixel by projected Keplerian velocity to common velocity, bin into 4 au annuli, average; fit Gaussian per annulus

evidence.quote: The data were then binned into annuli with a width of 4 au and then averaged to increase the signal-to-noise ratio.
The data were then binned into annuli with a width of 4 au

fitting.value: Gaussian line profile with width and peak T_B

evidence.quote: A Gaussian line profile, characterised by a line width $\Delta V$ and the peak brightness temperature $T_B$, was fit to each azimuthally averaged spectrum .

analysis_steps.goal: LTE fit of Tex and N(CS)

method.value: Rotation-diagram style fit of integrated fluxes with optical depth correction, pixel-by-pixel and on annuli

evidence.quote: allows us fit for $\left\{T_{\rm ex},\ N({\rm CS})\right\}$, self-consistently accounting for possible optical depth effects.

key_parameters.value: 256 walkers, 200 burn-in, 100 sampling steps; 10% flux systematic

evidence.quote: We used 256 walkers which took 200 steps to burn-in before taking an additional 100 to sample the posterior distribution.

assumptions.value: LTE; thermal broadening only for tau

evidence.quote: which can be calculated assuming only thermal broadening, a reasonable assumption given the low levels of turbulence previously reported.

fitting.value: emcee; uniform priors Tex 10-150 K, log N 9-14, tau<1

evidence.quote: To take this into account we include a prior that $\tau < 1$ for all lines.

method.value: Isothermal slab with RADEX grid (pyradex, 40 samples per axis, interpolated), sampled at fine resolution then Hanning smoothed; Gaussian-process noise

evidence.quote: a large grid in $\{T_{\rm kin},\, n({\rm H}_2),\, N({\rm CS}),\, \Delta V\}$ space was run using `pyradex`[^1], and linearly interpolated between points.

key_parameters.value: 13 free params per radius; 256 walkers, 1500 burn-in, 250 sampling steps

evidence.quote: Each fit consisted of 256 walkers, each taking 1500 steps for a burn-in period, then an additional 250 to sample the posterior distribution.

assumptions.value: Thermal H2 ortho-para ratio; slab geometry; no beam-smear correction

evidence.quote: We do not attempt to correct for such beam smear effects.

fitting.value: emcee; uniform priors T 10-150 K, log n 4-10, log N 9-14, log M -5 to 0 (also linear M 0-1)

evidence.quote: We additionally run a set of models where we fit for $\mathcal{M}$ rather than $\log_{10}\mathcal{M}$ for which we impose a prior of $\mathcal{M} = \mathcal{U}(0,\ 1)$.

validation.value: Compared with LTE results; grid interpolation checked; Matern-3/2 vs SHO kernels

findings_qualitative.value: CS column density shows knees at 90 au and 160 au; azimuthally symmetric structure

why_this_method.value: Multiple transitions break degeneracy between temperature and column density

evidence.quote: the degeneracy between column density and temperature could not be broken without assuming an underlying physical structure.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Simple harmonic oscillator noise kernel tested, no significant difference
